gloss: on bad terms; not getting along

definitions.gloss: on bad terms; not getting along
definitions.explanation: Describes a relationship where two or more people do not get along well, whether due to conflict, personality clashes, or long-standing friction.

examples.japanese: あの{二人|ふたり}は{仲|なか}が{悪|わる}い。
{兄弟|きょうだい}なのに{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}から{仲|なか}が{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: Even though they're siblings, they haven't gotten along since childhood.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{部署|ぶしょ}とは{仲|なか}が{悪|わる}くて、{会議|かいぎ}のたびに{意見|いけん}が{対立|たいりつ}する。
examples.english: We're on bad terms with the neighboring department, and opinions clash at every meeting.

notes:
The opposite of {仲|なか}がいい (to be on good terms). {仲|なか} refers to the quality of a relationship between people. This expression is used for any kind of interpersonal friction — between individuals, groups, organizations, or even countries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仲|なか}が{悪|わる}くなる: to become estranged
- {仲|なか}が{悪|わる}そう: they seem to not get along
- {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}: like cats and dogs (lit. dog-monkey relationship)

USAGE:
Can be used for both temporary conflicts and deep-seated animosity. The degree of the bad relationship depends on context. In formal contexts, {関係|かんけい}が{良|よ}くない or {折|お}り{合|あ}いが{悪|わる}い may be preferred.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不仲|ふなか}: discord, estrangement — a noun form meaning the same thing, slightly more formal
- {険悪|けんあく}: hostile, strained — describes a more seriously deteriorated atmosphere
- {仲|なか}がいい: on good terms — the direct antonym
